text: One Aimparency server holds many graphs: created there, mirrored from Git, or a local checkout
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: Aimparency is built for many graphs. Everyone just hosts Aimparency and manages users there. People can sign up and create graphs. For Commons Hub: a server where people host their graphs or mirror GitHub repos (the .bowman part at least). Using repos that are already checked out is an option for self-hosting.

Three kinds of graph on one server:
- created on the server by an account, with no repo
- mirrored from a Git URL (only .bowman, read-only, refreshed)
- a local checkout the server admin adds (self-hosting; ideas stay tracked next to the code)

Each graph has its own address on the server, so the MCP still connects to one address for one graph.

Today: a hosted server serves exactly one project (AIMPARENCY_PROJECT); the API identifies a project by its absolute path on the server; mirroring exists as "open from Git URL" (git-repository-cache.ts).

Assumed by Claude, not said by Felix: a graph created on the server is a .bowman folder in the server's data directory, so export to a repo and import from one stay a copy of that folder; the API names a graph by an id instead of a server path.

status.comment: Planned 2026-11-12 at Felix's request; not designed in detail, nothing built. Foundation for the other parts of d4203221.
